questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Managing Request Payload Limits?
options: Request bodies, parameters, and query strings arrive as untrusted values. Parse only the expected content type, enforce size limits, validate and normalize data, and return consistent client errors before business logic runs.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

questions.prompt: A change related to Managing Request Payload Limits appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?

Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
